newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE cocoa ends weaker on mixed selling.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE cocoa ends weaker on mixed selling.

text.p: London cocoa futures edged lower on mixed selling from origins, funds and trade houses but turnover was unspectacular, traders said.
Thursday's close marked the fourth consecutive loss as selling continued against dwindling demand. Origin selling was cited from Nigeria, Ivory Coast and Indonesia.
The benchmark March contract ended seven stg lower on the day at 985 stg a tonne, just off its session low of 983 stg, stepping closer to support seen around 975 stg.
The session started with mild gains, but prices soon reversed to negative territory, gaining downward momentum in the afternoon.
"It moved out of the range quite decisively. Now it's a question of where it finds support," said one trader.
But activity was sluggish ahead of Friday's trade dinner in Paris with total volume reaching 4,007 lots.
Dec/March switch traded at 27 and 25 stg.
European third quarter grinds are expected from Friday and forecasts point to a strong showing.
But the focus is more likely to be seized later in the month by Ivorian new crop arrivals which may provide a clue to the size of the harvest this year.
